coverage: United States land and the near-shore water strip covered by NAIP quarter-quads; Blue Marble and Landsat at small scales. Offshore coverage beyond the NAIP strip is not documented and must be checked visually (Looe Key, Fowey Rocks, Breakers reef).
licence: Public domain. USGS: "USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain." copyrightText: "USDA, USGS The National Map: Orthoimagery. Data refreshed June, 2024.v1.2"
attribution: Imagery: USGS The National Map, USDA NAIP
cors: not needed for display (loaded as ); header unverified
notes: Service metadata (fetched 30 Sep 2026): Web Mercator wkid 102100/3857, 256 px tiles, LODs 0 to 23 but serviceDescription says "visible to the 1:9,028 zoom scale" (maxScale 9027.977 = z16), so set maxNativeZoom 16 and let Leaflet upsample. USGS FAQ: NAIP is used at scales larger than 1:289,000, Landsat GLS 2000 at 1:1,150,000 to 1:289,000, Blue Marble above that. NAIP is 0.6 m to 1 m leaf-on imagery flown for agriculture, so water clarity and glint vary by flight. Tile path order is z/y/x (ArcGIS level/row/col). Replaces the unlicensed Esri World_Imagery hotlink.

No terms, AccessConstraints or Fees are published in the service or WMTS capabilities.
attribution: NOAA Office of Coast Survey, NOAA Chart Display Service. Not for navigation.
cors: not needed for display (loaded as ); header unverified
notes: THE TILE LEVELS ARE OFFSET BY 2. The cache's LOD 0 has resolution 39135.758 m (web mercator z2), so cache level L = web mercator zoom L+2. Probed 30 Sep 2026: tile/8/433/284 (the z10 Palm Beach tile) returned image content, tile/10/433/284 returned 404, tile/10/1732/1137 (z12) and tile/12/6930/4549 (z14) and tile/14/27720/18197 (z16) returned images, tile/15/55440/36395 (z17) and tile/16/.. (z18) returned 404 at Palm Beach. In Leaflet use zoomOffset:-2 with maxNativeZoom 16 (requests level 14 at most). Path order z/y/x is valid for the REST tile endpoint. The WMTS path .../MapServer/WMTS/tile/1.0.0/MarineChart_Services_NOAACharts/default/GoogleMapsCompatible/{z}/{y}/{x}.png behaves the same way (level 8 row 433 col 284 returned an image, level 10 returned 400) even though its capabilities list GoogleMapsCompatible from level 0, so it needs the same offset. The old RNC tile service (tileservice.charts.noaa.gov) was shut down (Hydro International: RNC Tile Service ended 1 October 2021); NCDS launched 8 March 2022 (NOAA bulletin). Coast Survey's GIS page lists this WMTS as the NCDS tile endpoint, plus REST https://gis.charttools.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/MCS/NOAAChartDisplay/MapServer/exts/MaritimeChartService/MapServer and WMS .../WMSServer for dynamic rendering. Offshore deep-zoom (z16) tiles timed out through WebFetch; the coordinator should confirm z16 offshore renders and not 404.

name: Sea surface temperature, MUR 0.01 deg daily (NASA JPL via CoastWatch ERDDAP WMS)
coverage: Global, gap-free analysis at 0.01 deg (about 1 km); latest time 2026-09-28T09:00Z when checked 30 Sep 2026 (one to two day lag).
licence: Dataset license: "These data are available free of charge under the JPL PO.DAAC data policy. The data may be used and redistributed for free but is not intended for legal use, since it may contain inaccuracies."
attribution: MUR SST: "These data were provided by JPL under support by NASA MEaSUREs program." Served by NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP
cors: unverified (WebFetch cannot read headers); needed only for fetch() of JSON or GetFeatureInfo
notes: ERDDAP WMS supports only EPSG:4326 (and CRS:84 in 1.3.0), not 3857. In Leaflet pass crs: L.CRS.EPSG4326 to L.tileLayer.wms; Leaflet then writes the 1.3.0 bbox in lat,lon order as ERDDAP requires. Per-tile stretch is under 1 px at z8 and above in Florida. Time: ERDDAP docs: "the default value is the last value in the dataset's 1D time array" and "'current' is interpreted as the last available time (recent or not)"; 'last' is not documented for WMS. Layer naming "datasetID:variableName" and the example GetMap URL are from the ERDDAP WMS documentation page. OPEN QUESTION: ERDDAP WMS colours use the dataset's default colour bar range; whether that gives useful contrast across Florida's 24 to 31 C range must be seen in a browser.
